clue.text: Top team's surprising defeat

blocks.note: up is at the top, the top position
a set is a team or group; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: A leading side has been beaten when nobody expected it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a league leader losing; read it as a word for top followed by a word for team.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is a result where the favourite unexpectedly loses.

clue.text: Peacekeepers argue over having the power to be unfair

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the next

blocks.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
to reason is to argue a case
able means having the power or capacity

explanation.surface: United Nations troops dispute whether they may act unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreasonable demand is one that is not fair or justified, beyond what is sensible.

clue.text: Backed journalist following games, including on horseback

indicators.note: following puts the journalist after the rest
including means the word for games holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: sport is games collectively
a jockey who is up is riding, mounted on a horse
ED, short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A racing reporter put money on a horse after the games, including the riding events.
explanation.walkthrough: Backed looks like betting; it means helped. A jockey is said to be up when riding in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone is to back them, giving help or encouragement.

clue.text: The newspaper caused offence

blocks.note: taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper article upset its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Offence reads as hurt feelings; it is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a criminal offence, so theft is an example of one.

clue.text: Before six, the French woman had showered

indicators.note: before says the French article comes first, ahead of the Roman numeral

blocks.note: la is the feminine French for the
six in Roman numerals
the pronoun for a woman
had contracts to 'd, as in she'd

explanation.surface: Someone notes what a Frenchwoman did before six o'clock: she had a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads showered as washing; here it means gave generously, as gifts are showered on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish praise or gifts on someone is to shower them with it, giving in abundance.

clue.text: Get ready to attack false story during interval

blocks.note: a lie is a false story
in means during, as in in the night
a wait is an interval of time

explanation.surface: Someone prepares an ambush, spreading a falsehood in the break.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide and prepare to ambush someone, an idiom for readying an attack.

clue.text: Ban from competitive tobogganing

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from racing toboggans.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a prohibition or a refusal to allow something, so a ban.

clue.text: Stays put in seats with little room to move

definitions.text: in seats with little room to move

blocks.note: first meaning: holds firm and does not move or act

blocks.clueFragment: in seats with little room to move
blocks.note: second, literal meaning: sitting squeezed into cramped seating

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally, a person wedged into a narrow seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remain where you are and take no action, waiting things out.

clue.text: Diplomat creates resentment about opposition leader

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of the word it follows
about means surrounding, so the word for resentment goes round the letter

blocks.note: envy is resentment of another's luck
the first letter of opposition

explanation.surface: A diplomat stirs up bitterness about the leader of the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent on a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Typical MP

blocks.note: first meaning: characteristic of a class, serving as an example
second meaning: an elected member of Parliament who acts for constituents

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that read as a jibe at politicians are separate meanings of one long word; MP is a Member of Parliament in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a sample that stands for its kind and a noun for an elected delegate.

clue.text: Secure support for a new name for news bulletin

indicators.note: in a down answer a support sits underneath, so this word goes below the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a noun is a naming word in grammar
to cement is to secure or bind firmly

explanation.surface: Someone wants funding for a new name for a news programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Secure support reads as obtaining backing; secure is a verb that ends up at the foot of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement of news, such as a bulletin read out.

clue.text: Taking on a party with power can get gruelling initially

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
a tin is a can
the first letter of gruelling

explanation.surface: Taking on a party in power could become an exhausting task at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Can looks like a verb meaning is able to; it is the noun, a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a child, a policy or a pet means taking it on as your own responsibility.

clue.text: Extremely significant "yes" vote reversed refusal to remain

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters
reversed tells us to write the word for refusal from back to front

blocks.note: the outside letters of significant
aye or ay is a vote in favour, as in the ayes have it
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A vote that could have been decisive was overturned, and someone refuses to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a referendum result being overturned; ST, AY and ON join to give STAY ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain in a place or post after others leave or after the expected time.

clue.text: Unmanageable without help?

blocks.note: first meaning: out of control
second, playful meaning: a hand is help, so being without one is being out of it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading, where hand means a helper, as in give me a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation or person that has slipped beyond control.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Romeo often got overlooked

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sadly, Romeo was frequently ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo looks like Shakespeare's lover; it is the radio code word for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been neglected or left out of mind, so passed over.

clue.text: Dissolute beach dude in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wild-living surfer has got himself into a scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: Debauched describes someone given to excessive indulgence, morally loose and depraved.

clue.text: Energy and enthusiasm got us dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move around and swap places, so the two words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Dancing gave us a burst of energy and enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty zest and relish in doing something, so lively vigour and keenness.

clue.text: Does nothing to get brown back between legs

indicators.note: back says the colour word is written in the opposite direction
between puts the turned word inside the word for legs

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
legs of a journey or race are stages

explanation.surface: A sunbather lazes about to get a tan on the backs of the legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Legs reads as limbs; it means sections of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stagnates stops moving or developing, becoming idle and inactive.

clue.text: Real fuss over dead tree

indicators.note: to fuss over something is to fiddle with it, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Someone makes a genuine fuss about a tree that has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuss reads as a noun in the surface; it works as a verb on the word before it, and dead adds one more letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a deciduous tree of the birch family that grows near water.

clue.text: Regularly tour Belgium and Spain with coach as transport

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first and third letters of tour
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
E is the vehicle code for Spain (España); and simply joins
to coach is to train; with joins it on

explanation.surface: A coach tour of Belgium and Spain is a regular way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests a bus; it is the verb meaning instruct. A tube train runs on the London Underground, known as the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube train is an underground railway carriage, a means of getting around London.

clue.text: Cream is not adulterated with oil

indicators.note: adulterated means corrupted by mixing, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a cosmetic cream has not been contaminated with oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface separates not from oil with adulterated; both words together form the mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a skin cream or liquid preparation applied to the body.

clue.text: Woods for a wild cat?

blocks.note: surface reading: forests where a wild feline lives
setter's reading: the famous golfer surnamed Woods has a first name that is also a big striped cat

explanation.walkthrough: Woods looks like woodland habitat; the capital W is the clue that it is the golfer, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer's first name is also the large striped wild cat of Asia.

clue.text: After university I take steps to follow good advice

indicators.note: after places the word for university later in the answer than the next piece named
to follow puts the preceding group after the abbreviation that ends the clue's wordplay

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written
to dance is to take steps to music

explanation.surface: A graduate says that after university they follow good advice step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: Good comes first, then U, then I, then DANCE: the indicators push each later piece behind good.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is direction or counsel given to help someone decide, so it is advice.

clue.text: Without rain initially the German river becomes less full of water

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of rain
without here means outside, so the German article wraps round the letter

blocks.note: die is a German word for the
the first letter of rain
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: With no rain, the German river runs lower.
explanation.walkthrough: Without seems to mean lacking; it is the old sense outside, so DIE goes round R before river is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier is the comparative of dry, describing something holding less moisture.

clue.text: Hasty strike after changing sides at the top

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so swapping sides at the top turns the first letter from one into the other

blocks.note: to lash is to strike with a whip

explanation.surface: A rushed walkout after the leadership switched allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left becomes R for right at the head of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one made hastily, without enough thought.

clue.text: Author's murderer goes after girl

indicators.note: goes after says the killer's name is placed behind the girl's

blocks.note: a girl's name
John Christie was a notorious English murderer of 10 Rillington Place

explanation.surface: A writer's killer pursues a young woman, a fitting plot for a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for is; the girl's first name and the killer's surname make the author's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English crime writer who created Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: Made a grinding noise to turn on central heating in about December

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the month's abbreviation is read backwards
in puts the first pieces inside the turned-round abbreviation

blocks.note: to run a machine is to turn it on and operate it
CH is the abbreviation for central heating
Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: An old boiler ground noisily when the heating was switched on around December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About December' looks like a time phrase; about turns the month's abbreviation round. To run an engine is to have it switched on and working.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crunched when it made a crushing, grating sound, like feet on gravel.

clue.text: Beginning to improve during break, so try to pass again

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of the word that follows
during means within a period, so the letter sits inside the word for break

blocks.note: the first letter of improve
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A student starts to improve during the holidays, so takes the exam once more.
explanation.walkthrough: A resit is the British term for retaking a failed exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit an exam is to sit it a second time, hoping to pass after failing.
